## Part 1: On paper

::: {#exr-geometric}
## The geometric series

1. Show that, for $q \neq 1$,
   $$
     \sum_{k=0}^{n} q^k = \frac{1 - q^{n+1}}{1 - q}.
   $$

1. Compute the value of $0.999\ldots = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} 9 \cdot 10^{-k}$.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Hint
Multiply the sum by $1 - q$.
:::

::: {.lm-solution}
1. Multiplying the sum $s_n$ by $1 - q$, all terms but the first and the last cancel: $(1 - q) s_n = 1 - q^{n+1}$.

1. For $|q| < 1$, $q^{n+1} \to 0$, so $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} q^k = 1 / (1 - q)$. With $q = 1/10$:
   $$
     \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} 9 \cdot 10^{-k} = \frac{9}{10} \cdot \frac{1}{1 - 1/10} = 1.
   $$
:::
:::

## Part 2: In R

Download the [work files](06-series-exercises.zip) and unzip them into your project folder.

::: {#exr-alternating}
## The alternating harmonic series

The alternating harmonic series converges to $\ln 2$:
$$
  \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{k+1}}{k} = 1 - \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} - \ldots = \ln 2.
$$

### Implementation

Implement the function `partial_sums(n)`, which returns the vector of the partial sums $s_1, \ldots, s_n$.

::: {.lm-scaffold}
```{r}
partial_sums <- function(n) {
  # ...
}
```
:::

::: {.lm-solution}
```{r}
partial_sums <- function(n) {
  k <- 1:n
  cumsum((-1)^(k + 1) / k)
}
```
:::

### Errors

Compute the errors of $s_{10}$, $s_{100}$ and $s_{1000}$. How many terms are needed for one more correct digit? Compare with the geometric series from @exr-geometric.

::: {.lm-solution}
```{r}
sums <- partial_sums(1000)
ns <- c(10, 100, 1000)
data.frame(n = ns, error = abs(sums[ns] - log(2)))
```

The error is about $1 / (2n)$: one more correct digit needs ten times as many terms. The geometric series with $q = 1/10$ gains one digit with each term.
:::
:::
